metadata.title: Theory of Mind, Depth Psychology and Psychotherapy Context
metadata.description: A curated semantic context module linking contemporary theory of mind and mentalization with major depth-psychological, psychoanalytic, humanistic and process-oriented thinkers.
metadata.intended_use: Feed into an agentic AI as structured background context, source discovery and relationship mapping. The linked resources should be consulted when greater depth or verification is required.
metadata.epistemic_note: Theories in psychology differ substantially in empirical support. Historical and clinical theories should be represented as theoretical frameworks rather than automatically treated as established biological or neuroscientific facts.

reasoning_guidance: Distinguish historical influence from current empirical support.
Do not collapse different schools into a single theory of mind.
When comparing theorists, identify both conceptual continuities and disagreements.
Treat concepts such as archetypes, collective unconscious, dreambody, id/ego/superego and the Real/Symbolic/Imaginary as concepts within their respective theoretical systems.
Where contemporary cognitive science, developmental psychology or neuroscience provides relevant evidence, distinguish it from psychodynamic interpretation.
Use the relationship map to retrieve adjacent modules when a question crosses theoretical traditions.

topics.name: Theory of Mind
topics.summary: Theory of mind, also called mindreading or often mentalizing, concerns the capacity to attribute mental states such as beliefs, intentions, desires and feelings to other people and use those attributions to understand or predict behaviour.

sources.title: Theory of Mind
sources.use: Detailed conceptual and philosophical introduction to theory of mind and mindreading.

sources.title: The social neuroscience of mentalizing: challenges and recommendations
sources.publisher: Current Opinion in Psychology / PubMed Central
sources.use: Research-oriented overview of mentalizing, measurement, neuroscience and methodological limitations.

sources.title: The Neurobiology of Mentalizing
sources.use: Bridge between psychological mentalization theory and contemporary neuroscience.

topics.name: Sigmund Freud
topics.summary: Freud developed psychoanalysis and a model of psychological life centred on unconscious processes, conflict, defence, early development, dreams, transference and the dynamic interaction of psychological forces.

sources.title: Freud and the Psychodynamic Perspective
sources.use: Accessible overview that also places Freud's ideas in contemporary psychology.

sources.title: Freud 101
sources.use: Orientation to Freud's life, work, major ideas and interdisciplinary legacy.

topics.name: Carl Gustav Jung
topics.summary: Jung developed analytical psychology, expanding depth psychology through concepts including complexes, archetypes, the collective unconscious, psychological types, active imagination and individuation.

sources.title: Carl Gustav Jung
sources.use: Detailed account of Jung's intellectual development and central concepts.

sources.title: Jung, Carl Gustav (1875–1961)
sources.use: Scholarly summary of Jung's theory of archetypes and personality.

topics.name: Alfred Adler
topics.summary: Adler's individual psychology emphasises purposive striving, feelings of inferiority and compensation, style of life, social interest, belonging and the individual as an integrated person embedded within a social world.

sources.title: Individual Psychology
sources.use: Concise authoritative definition of Adlerian individual psychology.

sources.title: Alfred Adler | Vision and Lasting Impact
sources.use: Overview of Adler's social, community and therapeutic orientation.

sources.title: The Drive for Self: Alfred Adler and the Founding of Individual Psychology
sources.use: Historical and conceptual discussion of Adler's influence.

topics.name: James Hillman
topics.summary: Hillman developed archetypal psychology as a post-Jungian approach that shifts emphasis from ego-centred explanation toward image, imagination, soul, mythology, multiplicity and the psychological life of culture and the world.

sources.title: Archetypal Psychology — course description
sources.use: Compact academic description of Hillman's archetypal psychology and its characteristic moves.

sources.title: Dr. James Hillman
sources.publisher: The Dallas Institute of Humanities and Culture
sources.use: Places Hillman's work in its intellectual and cultural context.

sources.title: James Hillman
sources.use: Guide to Hillman's major works and recurring themes.

topics.name: Arnold Mindell
topics.summary: Mindell developed Processwork from Jungian psychology, dreamwork and attention to body experience. It follows verbal and non-verbal signals across inner experience, relationships, groups, altered states and conflict, with awareness itself functioning as a central method.

sources.title: Process-Oriented Psychology
sources.use: Comprehensive first-party introduction to Processwork theory, history and practice.

sources.title: What is Processwork?
sources.use: Concise description of Processwork's Jungian origins and development.

sources.title: Process
sources.use: Focused explanation of the central Processwork concept of process.

topics.name: Melanie Klein
topics.summary: Klein extended psychoanalysis through close attention to early object relations, unconscious phantasy, splitting, projective processes and the evolving internal world of the infant.

sources.title: Melanie Klein
sources.use: Detailed professional overview of Klein's development and key concepts.

sources.title: Object Relations Theory
sources.use: Concise definition of the broader theoretical tradition associated with Klein and others.

topics.name: Donald Winnicott
topics.summary: Winnicott emphasised the development of a lived sense of self within a facilitating environment, including the roles of holding, play, transitional phenomena, creativity and adaptation to the infant's needs.

sources.title: Donald Woods Winnicott
sources.use: Substantive overview of Winnicott's theoretical development.

sources.title: Introduction to the work of Donald Winnicott
sources.use: Maps Winnicott's major concepts into a coherent learning sequence.

topics.name: John Bowlby
topics.summary: Bowlby integrated psychoanalytic questions about relationships with ethology and developmental thinking, proposing attachment as an evolved behavioural system through which children seek proximity and security from caregivers.

sources.title: Attachment Theory
sources.use: Authoritative concise definition and attribution to Bowlby and Ainsworth.

sources.title: The Science and Clinical Practice of Attachment Theory
sources.use: Contemporary framing of attachment science, historical foundations and clinical applications.

topics.name: Peter Fonagy and Mentalization
topics.summary: Mentalization theory links attachment, development, affect regulation and the capacity to understand behaviour in terms of intentional mental states. It provides an important conceptual bridge between psychodynamic thought and contemporary theory-of-mind research.

sources.title: The Neurobiology of Mentalizing
sources.use: Scholarly bridge between mentalization theory, development and neuroscience.

topics.name: Jacques Lacan
topics.summary: Lacan reinterpreted Freud through linguistics, structuralism and philosophy, emphasising language, desire, subject formation and the relation between the Imaginary, Symbolic and Real.

sources.title: Jacques Lacan
sources.use: Detailed and current scholarly introduction to Lacan's major concepts.

sources.title: Jacques Lacan
sources.use: Extensive alternative introduction emphasising Lacan's philosophical and psychoanalytic project.

topics.name: Carl Rogers
topics.summary: Rogers developed person-centred therapy around the proposition that a therapeutic relationship characterised by empathic understanding, congruence and unconditional positive regard can facilitate psychological growth and greater self-directed functioning.

sources.title: Carl Rogers, PhD
sources.use: Authoritative introduction to Rogers and his influence.

sources.title: Person-Centered Psychotherapies, Second Edition
sources.use: Contemporary overview of person-centred theory, mechanisms, evidence and practice.

topics.name: Viktor Frankl
topics.summary: Frankl's logotherapy centres psychological meaning, responsibility and freedom of response, proposing a will to meaning as a major human motivational orientation.

sources.title: What is Logotherapy?
sources.publisher: Viktor E. Frankl Institute of America
sources.use: Clear overview of the central principles of Frankl's logotherapy.
